content:
Philip Ruddock, a former Liberal minister, has been appointed by cabinet to review whether Australian law adequately protects freedom of religion.

The review appears aimed at reducing conflict over proposed religious freedom amendments linked to the same-sex marriage bill, though Treasurer Scott Morrison said it should not replace those amendments.

Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull said it was important to examine religious freedom carefully in light of the yes vote in the marriage equality campaign and the forthcoming legislation.

There is disagreement within the government over timing and scope: some conservatives want a separate religious freedom bill next year, while others want it considered alongside the marriage bill.

Ruddock must report by 31 March. Turnbull said reforms should be approached cautiously because of the risk of unintended consequences, and praised Ruddock’s suitability due to his experience as Australia’s special envoy for human rights.
